evidence.quote: let private onShelf (library: Library) (copies: Copy list) = copies |> List.filter (fun c -> not (library.Loans.ContainsKey c.Id)) |> List.length
|> List.filter (fun b -> contains b.Title || contains b.Author)
let copies = library.Copies |> Map.toList |> List.map snd |> List.filter (fun c -> c.Book = b.Id)

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The change adds no Tier 2 code. The search match rule (title or author contains the text, ignoring case) and the definition of 'on shelf' (not in Loans) are written directly in the Tier 3 Views module. Both are read-only projection logic, and there is no competing Tier 2 definition, so they don't contradict anything. Unknown-book handling does go through Tier 2 (Catalog.findBook), and branch copies go through Catalog.copiesAt. The copies-of-a-book lookup and the on-shelf predicate are still re-derived in Tier 3 instead of being asked of Tier 2. Tier 4 (CLI) only renders. Score 1 rather than 0, because this is view-level counting and no legality decision is made.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is added. The use cases run through the existing `query ports` helper, and the pure view functions take a Library value. The CLI only formats strings and calls use cases. Tier 1/2 is untouched, and there is no clock, I/O or presentation-to-Tier-2 call.

evidence.quote: library.Copies |> Map.toList |> List.map snd |> List.filter (fun c -> c.Book = b.Id)

ARC-REV-03.rationale: 'Copies of a book' is restated in two new views (search and bookCopies) instead of being defined once in Catalog, which is where copiesAt already lives for branches. The two copies agree. 'On shelf' is defined once, in the shared onShelf helper, and is reused by search and branchSummaries. The older shelf view derives loan state separately, but that is existing code. The result is one restated fact with agreeing copies.

evidence.quote: |> List.filter (fun b -> contains b.Title || contains b.Author || b.Isbn = text)
|> List.filter (fun c -> c.Book = b.Id && (branch |> Option.forall (fun id -> c.Branch = id)))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: Branch validity is delegated to Tier 2 (`Catalog.findBranch id library`). The new match rule (ISBN equality), the branch-copy membership test and the 'omit books with no copy at the branch' rule are all written in the Tier 3 Views module. Tier 2 already offers Catalog.copiesAt, but this code doesn't use it. This is the same pattern as change set 1, with slightly more rule-like logic added in Tier 3. None of it contradicts Tier 2. Tier 4 (the CLI) only passes the branch through and renders it.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: No new effect is added. The branch option is passed to the pure `Views.search` through the existing `query ports`. Only the CLI formatting and parsing change in Tier 4, and nothing is read from the clock or from I/O below Tier 4.

evidence.quote: c.Book = b.Id && (branch |> Option.forall (fun id -> c.Branch = id))
contains b.Title || contains b.Author || b.Isbn = text

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The 'copies shelved at a branch' fact is restated as an inline `c.Branch = id` test, while Catalog.copiesAt exists and branchSummaries uses it. The 'copies of a book' filter still appears in both search and bookCopies. The copies agree, so they don't contradict each other. The usage text `search <text> [<branch>]` appears in both the help list and the error message. That comes from the existing shared `usage`, which the diff's test expects to match, so I read it as a single definition. The result is a restated fact with agreeing copies.
